hadiths.english_translation: Narrated by Yahya, from Malik: What is the matter with men who have intercourse with their slave women and then leave them? hadiths.english_translation: Narrated by Malik, from Amr ibn Yahya al-Mazini, from his father: Al-Dahhak ibn Khalifah wanted to lead an irrigation channel through the land of Muhammad ibn Maslamah, but Muhammad refused. Al-Dahhak said to him: Why do you prevent me when it benefits you - you drink from it first and last, and it does not harm you? Muhammad refused. Al-Dahhak spoke about this to Umar ibn al-Khattab. Umar called Muhammad and ordered him to let it pass. Muhammad said: No. Umar said: Why do you prevent your brother from what benefits him and is beneficial to you - you drink from it first and last and it does not harm you? Muhammad said: By Allah, no. Umar said: By Allah, it will pass through even if upon your belly. Then Umar ordered him to let it pass, and al-Dahhak did so.

critical_findings: Ibn Shihab al-Zuhri appears in multiple chains using عَنْ transmission. While he is classified as a mudallis (category 3), he is highly reliable overall and this does not significantly affect the grade of these hadiths.
Hadith 9458 contains a weak transmission link (balaghani) through Abdullah ibn Abi Bakr, classified as 'Weak But Might Be Acceptable'.
Most hadiths in this file are from Malik's Muwatta', with Yahya ibn Yahya al-Tamimi as the primary narrator from Malik.
Several hadiths feature legal rulings attributed to Umar ibn al-Khattab (mawquf), particularly regarding property and water rights.
Amr ibn Yahya al-Mazini appears as an intermediate narrator in multiple chains with Saduq/Sadooq grade - reliable but not of the highest level.
